hints.title: Two-Pass Equality Partitioning
hints.text: Equality is an equivalence relation. Group variables connected by double equals into the same set before verifying inequalities.

hints.title: Contradiction Detection on Inequalities
hints.text: In the second pass, verify all exclamation-equals equations. If two variables asserted to be unequal belong to the same connected component, a contradiction exists.

hints.title: Alphabet Disjoint Sets
hints.text: Initialize parent array of size 26. First pass: for equations with ==, union the two variable indices. Second pass: for equations with exclamation-equals, if find(a) equals find(b), return False. If all pass, return True.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Processing equations out of order without grouping equivalences first causes false negatives on transitive chains like a==b, b==c, a!=c.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Since variables are 26 lowercase English letters, union-find takes O(1) space and strictly O(N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should clearly explain the 2-pass strategy: process all equalities first, then test all inequalities.
complexity.notes: Equations always have length 4 with format a==b or a!=b.
